method: Fresh independent read-only review after the recorded freeze. Fully read all deployment Python/shell/Go executable modules, all deployment standard/root/helper test sources, all tooling JavaScript/Python/TypeScript sources and tests, workflow YAML, project configuration, and all assigned Markdown/legal documents. Followed source contracts for initialization/resume; UID ownership and privileged helper boundaries; source and release sealing; safe filesystem publication, fsync and journals; service stop/readiness/rollback; account, provider and control updates; DNS credentials, pinned Caddy/Go builds, explicit loopback acquisition proxy, DNS-01 on high public ports, TLS health and renewal-state claims; archive extraction and download provenance; workspace file/index/commit/worktree recovery; test discovery, isolated environments, skip and per-file accounting, cross-platform CI aggregation, full-test authorization and release reports. Cross-checked current test assertions and operational commands against the implementation rather than treating existing reports as success evidence. Structurally parsed every pnpm-lock record: 336 packages and snapshots, 623 dependency/optional edges, 21 direct dependencies, pinned SDK/Zod overrides and platform bindings; verified integrity fields and resolved edge targets. Parsed all 1510 go.sum entries for valid unique module/version/hash records and coverage of all 166 go.mod modules, and inspected the complete pinned Go module recipe. Fully read the smaller assigned feature-evidence JSON documents for scope and limitations; semantically parsed the 326KB capability inventory, reading every unique method/group/workflow assessment, validating all 178 method names and parameter imports against current ClientRequest.ts, all 175 JSON variant pointers, all classification/status counts, all 50 group memberships, 15 extra workflows, 532 non-audit path references and 156 historical report metadata records. Historical source hashes and report references were treated as dated documentation, not as correctness proof; prior audit reports and previous checkouts/history were not opened. Verified every one of the 1901 inventory content hashes, exact path set and snapshot digest at start and again immediately before this report. This complete result denotes completed review of the assigned 172 files, not live deployment or external-service acceptance. No source files were changed, no remote operation was made, and no full test suite was run.
limitations: Static audit on the Windows review host; Linux root/systemd process, UID, mount, DNS provider, ACME issuance/renewal, proxy reachability and real-account behavior were not executed or certified by this reviewer.
No targeted Python test result is claimed: available Python commands resolved to WindowsApps stubs. No full test suite was run, respecting the two-clean-audit gate.
Dependency locks were structurally and contractually reviewed; this review did not perform remote package provenance retrieval or a current vulnerability database audit.

Capability and feature-evidence documents retain historical hashes, platform skips and external-service limits. Their historical pass fields were not accepted as proof of the current frozen source. Runtime and web implementation outside this assigned scope was cross-referenced only where needed and remains owned by the other independent reviewers.
